items.title: HUGE: Dell Picks India to Test Whether Industry Can Train Workers Faster Than Universities Can
items.summary:
Dell Udaan aims to prepare 23,000 young Indians for careers in AI and electronics manufacturing. Learn how this initiative targets workforce development across key technology corridors.

Dell Technologies has launched this national skilling program to bridge the talent gap in high-growth sectors. By partnering with government-initiated institutions, the program focuses on practical training that aligns with the evolving needs of the industry. This effort is designed to equip students with the necessary technical skills to succeed in modern AI roles and complex manufacturing environments.

With Dell employees contributing over 2,000 hours of mentorship, the initiative provides hands-on guidance for participants. This workforce development approach ensures that the training remains relevant to current market demands. We examine the structural impact of this program on India's technology ecosystem and the long-term benefits for the next generation of professionals.

items.title: HUGE: Karnataka Is Asking 500 French Companies to Set Up Factories and Labs Across the State
items.summary:
Karnataka investment is shifting as Minister MB Patil visits France to pitch the state for manufacturing and aerospace.

Karnataka Industries Minister MB Patil is in France to broaden the state's economic profile beyond its traditional IT sector. The mission focuses on securing new partnerships in manufacturing and research, specifically targeting French industrial capital to boost local production capabilities.

The proposal includes expansion talks with firms like Roquette and bioMérieux, alongside negotiations with Hutchinson to strengthen aerospace manufacturing within the region. While these meetings aim to attract significant resources for the 2027 Global Investors Meet, the focus remains on securing concrete factory expansions and R&D commitments rather than just soft agreements.

items.title: The Word That Bends an LLM the Most Isn't a Noun (with Luis Serrano)
items.summary:
#transformers #attentionmechanism #GRPO

In Episode #1025, Dr. Luis Serrano (Founder of Serrano Academy) joins @JonKrohnLearns to explain the paper he co-authored on the curved spacetime of transformer architectures, in which attention stops being a lookup table and becomes something closer to gravity: words bend the space around them, and the embedding of "bank" visibly curves toward "river" as it travels through the layers of the network. In this episode, he recreates Eddington’s 1919 eclipse experiment inside a transformer, draws the line between an LLM workflow and an actual agent, explains why agent evaluation is a step harder than evaluating an essay, and gives the cleanest account of GRPO you will hear.

This episode is brought to you by: 
• ODSC, the Open Data Science Conference: https://odsc.ai/west/
• Anthropic: https://claude.ai/superdata 
• Gurobi: https://www.superdatascience.com/gurobi
• Y Carrot: https://www.ycarrot.com/

Interested in sponsoring a SuperDataScience Podcast episode? Email natalie@superdatascience.com for sponsorship information.

In this episode you will learn:
• (00:00:00) Introduction
• (00:10:53) What changed, and what survived, between the two editions of Grokking Machine Learning
• (00:28:48) Word gravity: how attention pulls "bank" toward "river"
• (00:43:44) Why RAG is an LLM workflow rather than an agent
• (00:53:08) The two-by-two that explains why GRPO powers reasoning models

Additional materials: https://www.superdatascience.com/1025

items.title: Building Europe's AI Stack — Inside the Barcelona Supercomputing Center
items.summary:
We sat down with the Barcelona Supercomputing Center to talk about what it really takes to turn a continent's scientific ambition into an AI powerhouse.

BSC hosts MareNostrum 5 — one of the largest supercomputers in Europe. But raw compute is just the start. The BSC AI Factory, backed by the European Commission, is doing something harder: compressing the journey from idea to deployable AI product for the startups and SMEs who can't afford to wait.

The model is simple in concept, hard to execute: energy → chips → infrastructure → models → applications. Five layers. One coherent stack.

items.title: How Many Narrow AIs Could Behave Like One Superintelligence - Daniel Kokotajlo and Thomas Larsen
items.summary:
Could slowing AI development make superintelligence safer? Daniel Kokotajlo and Thomas Larsen of the AI Futures Project join Tim Scarfe to examine AI 2040: Plan A, a proposal to buy time before AI exceeds human control.

SPONSOR:
---
Cyber Fund built the Monastery to help founders ship products that were impossible a year ago.
Apply now: https://cyber.fund
---

After revisiting AI 2027 and the limits of forecasting, they ask what happens when AI can automate research and sustain an economy without human workers. Tim challenges the case for general models and asks whether intelligence alone explains power. Plan A proposes an initial pause to build safety infrastructure, then cautious development up to the strongest AI that can still be reliably controlled. The discussion tests the distinction between control and alignment, the case for public AI research, and whether the US and China could enforce a slowdown. It ends with the evidence that would change their forecasts.

items.summary:
OpenAI inference costs are surging as research teams shift toward machine labor, with daily spending reaching new highs for heavy users.

We analyze the evolving economics of AI development, where median users now consume over $600 daily in compute resources, while power users are exceeding $7,000. This data highlights a clear transition in how organizations manage AI agents to handle routine tasks, allowing human researchers to focus exclusively on complex challenges that require nuanced problem-solving. 

Understanding these OpenAI inference patterns is critical for any enterprise leader or developer assessing the long-term cost of scaling automated workflows. We break down what this reliance on machine labor means for the future of AI research and operational budgets.

Bengaluru-based spacetech startup Pixxel closed a landmark $100 million Series C funding round led by Temasek and Seraphim Space, bringing its total raised capital to $195 million. The fundraise marks the single-largest private investment in India's space-tech sector to date, accelerating Pixxel's Honeybee satellite constellation, Aurora Earth intelligence platform, and sovereign space systems. Globally, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang declared that AGI has officially arrived with the release of OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra model. Meanwhile, TCS subsidiary HyperVault announced a ₹70,000 crore, 1 GW AI data center campus in Hyderabad, Spotify cut Claude Code token costs by 90% via smart model routing, Google DeepMind backed four Indian climate AI teams, D K Shivakumar pitched Bengaluru as a US-India tech hub, and Calibo Executive Chairman Raj Vattikutti joins us live.

This is your Front Page LIVE, bringing you sharp analysis of the biggest technology, business, policy and economic stories shaping India and the world.
